info.name: Inventory · Masters (Warehouse / Zone / Rack / Shelf / Product Flags)
info.description:
34 endpoints under /api/inventory.

PROPOSED — the five tables are not migrated yet, so every call 500s until `php artisan migrate` has run.

Run **Auth → Login** first; the script writes {{token}} and the collection auth is already Bearer {{token}}.

Then run the folders in order: creating a warehouse sets {{warehouse_id}}, creating a zone sets {{zone_id}}, and so on down the chain. Each level's /options feeds the next level's dropdown.

**No codes are ever sent.** WH-014, ZN-003, RK-001 and PF-004 are 'PREFIX-' plus the zero-padded id, and RK-001-SH-01 is the rack code plus the level. They come back on every row as wh_code / zone_code / rack_code / shelf_code / flag_code.

**status is 0 or 1**, not a word. Nothing is hard-deleted once it has children — the toggle is how a location is retired, and deactivating cascades downwards.

**Every list returns the same envelope**: { status, data[], tabs: { all, active, inactive }, meta: { page, per_page, total, last_page } }. The tab counts are taken before the search narrows anything.

exec: console.warn('no token in the response — check the credentials');

request.description:
Run this FIRST. The test script writes the token into the collection variable, so every other request authenticates on its own.

auth is noauth here on purpose: sending a stale bearer token to /login is harmless but noisy.

The grid. tab counts All / Active / Inactive BEFORE the search narrows anything, so typing in the box never changes them.

Filters: tab, q, wh_type, city, state, page, per_page (default 10, max 100).

Each row carries zones_count and racks_count as subqueries — a page of ten costs two extra queries, not twenty.

Active warehouses only, with the four AUTO fields the Zone and Rack forms show beside the picker: wh_type, area_sqft and location.

This is the first step of the cascade — warehouse → zone → rack → shelf.

formdata.description: JPG, PNG or PDF · up to 5 MB · optional

request.description:
multipart/form-data, because of the business-card upload. Send it as plain JSON instead when there is no card.

wh_type is the field with consequences: 'own' means the site is zoned, racked and scanned to a shelf; 'tpl' means a third party holds the stock and a put-away is a summary drop.

No code is sent — WH-014 is derived from the id.
Adds free_area_sqft: the warehouse area minus every zone already in it. The Add Zone form reads it to show how much room is left.

formdata.description: JPG, PNG or PDF · up to 5 MB · optional

request.description: POST, not PUT — PHP does not populate $_FILES on a PUT. A new card replaces the old one only once it is on disk, so a failed upload cannot lose the existing file.

1 = active, 0 = inactive.

Deactivating CASCADES: every zone and rack under it goes inactive too, otherwise they would stay on the put-away picker under a warehouse nobody can use.

409 once it holds zones — the status toggle is how a warehouse is retired. Deleting one would orphan every rack and shelf beneath it.

The business card is removed from disk with the row.
Filters: tab, q, warehouse_id, rack_mode, cold_chain, hazardous, page, per_page.

The Rack form's zone dropdown. rack_mode=rack because a rack can only go in a racked zone.

Sends the zone's cold_chain, hazardous and temperature range too — the Rack form shows all three as AUTO and validates its own toggles against them.

A racked zone sends NO capacity figures — its racks carry them. Sending storage_mode, litres or dimensions here is ignored: the server nulls the half the rack_mode does not use.

Guard: area_sqft must fit in what the warehouse has left. Only the server can see the other zones, so only the server can check it.

item.name: Create zone · WITHOUT rack, open floor

request.description:
No shelf to scan, so the zone states its own capacity. Every figure (floor_area, volume, usable_volume) is computed on the screen and stored as sent.

usable_pct is the share actually stackable once aisles and clearance come out — usable_volume is what planning reads, gross volume always overstates it.

A fridge is measured in litres, not dimensions. Sending both is rejected rather than ignored — a fridge saved with floor dimensions would show capacity it does not have.

cold_chain=1 requires BOTH temperatures, min below max, each between -80 and +60 °C.
Adds free_area_sqft — the zone area minus every rack already in it. The Add Rack form reads it.
409 if you switch a zone that already has racks to 'norack' — the racks are only reachable through a racked zone, so they would be stranded.
Deactivating cascades to its racks. Re-activating is refused while its warehouse is inactive — the zone would be reachable through a warehouse nobody can use.
409 once it holds racks.

Filters: tab, q, warehouse_id, zone_id, cold_chain, hazardous, page, per_page.

Each row carries shelves_count, capacity_kg, used_kg and load_pct — three subqueries for the whole page rather than three per row.
Active racks by warehouse or by zone — pass at least one. Returns height_cm already converted, which is the unit every shelf comparison is made in.

warehouse_id is NOT sent — it is taken from the zone, so the two can never disagree.

area_sqft is computed server-side from length × width × unit, not taken from the payload: it is the number the zone-capacity guard sums, so letting the client send it would let the client decide whether the rack fits.

Guards: the zone must be rack_mode=rack and active; the name must be unique inside it; cold_chain / hazardous cannot exceed what the zone allows; the footprint must fit in the zone's free area.
Adds free_height_cm and next_level_no, so the Add Shelf form opens already knowing its limits.
Shrinking a rack below the height its shelves already use is refused — the next shelf save would otherwise be impossible to reason about.
Deactivating cascades to its shelves. Re-activating is refused while its zone is inactive.
409 once it holds shelves.

The shelf drawer in one call: the levels, the KPI strip above them (levels, capacity_kg, used_kg, load_pct, boxes) and the rack's own limits including free_height_cm and next_level_no.

Not paginated — a rack has levels, not pages.

Nested under the rack because every rule it has to pass is a comparison against that rack: length and width are capped by the rack's, and height by what the shelves already stacked have left.

All of those are compared in CENTIMETRES whatever unit was typed, which is why height_cm is stored as well as height.

used_weight_kg and boxes_count are NOT accepted here — they belong to the SPI put-away. A master form that could set them would let someone mark a shelf empty while boxes are still on it.
occupancy (empty / partial / full / inactive) and load_pct are derived from used vs max, never stored — so they cannot contradict used_weight_kg.
max_weight_kg cannot drop below what is already stored on the shelf.
409 while boxes are still on it. Re-activating is refused while its rack is inactive.

Filters: tab, q, page, per_page.

Active flags for the picker on the SPI box-item form. That form holds its selection in a json column, so this master names and explains the labels — it does not own the assignment, and nothing cascades from here.
Two flags called 'Fragile' would be indistinguishable on the box form, so the name is unique per client.
Nothing cascades — a flag has no children.
Allowed outright, unlike the other four: a flag has no children to orphan.
